fallback.text: Five towns s, t, x, y and z are joined by one-way roads with costs (the network of Cormen et al., Introduction to Algorithms, Fig. 24.6). Dijkstra's algorithm settles the towns in the order s (0), y (5), z (7), t (8), x (9): it always settles the open town with the smallest known cost, then relaxes the roads leaving it. With the road s → t at cost 10 the cheapest route to x is s → y → t → x, cost 9. Lowering that road to 7 or less makes s → t → x the cheapest, at cost 8 or less. The picture shows the network when the algorithm has finished, with the cheapest routes from s drawn bold.
